hypotheses.mechanism: The current G9 prose/source surface uses syntactic forms not admitted by the checked-in G9 EBNF, so the grammar cannot be a faithful parser contract for the current candidate.
hypotheses.expected: Representative source lines containing >, <, union types, returns/includes, if, and postfix optional/or fail under the unmodified grammar.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The EBNF is intentionally only a partial illustrative grammar and a different canonical parser accepts the current source.
hypotheses.falsifier: The actual canonical parser/grammar parses the complete current G9 spec and roundtrips it without grammar extension or semantic loss.
hypotheses.result: Original grammar 2/10; eight source-used forms rejected.

hypotheses.mechanism: A minimal parser/grammar alignment can cover the observed G9 source forms without redesigning ClayCode semantics.
hypotheses.expected: Adding only source-used union/control/operator/postfix forms accepts the same corpus without changing rule meanings.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The syntactic mismatches hide deeper ambiguity that requires semantic redesign.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full-spec parse/roundtrip, type checking, or mutation tests expose ambiguous or contradictory meanings after the minimal grammar repair.
hypotheses.test: Same 10-case corpus under minimal aligned grammar.

hypotheses.mechanism: Existing typed records/rules/effect concepts are sufficient to encode the BASE-stage adaptive visual learner transition contract without a new language primitive.
hypotheses.expected: Trusted-tier admission, BRONZE rejection, candidate promotion, budget fallback, rollback and external commit authority can parse, lower and execute from ClayCode-like source.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Full H1 learner semantics require opaque host escape hatches or new primitives for version/provenance/replay/atomic promotion.
hypotheses.falsifier: A frozen H1 learner transition cannot be represented and differentially replayed through the full ClayCode compiler/runtime using existing semantic classes.
hypotheses.test: Prototype parser/compiler/lowering to Python plus separate-process execution.
hypotheses.result: 9/9 semantic cases passed; narrow prototype only.

hypotheses.mechanism: ClayCode should preserve computational expressibility while external effect authority is represented by non-textual, runtime-bound capability/authorization state.
hypotheses.expected: Programs may express destructive/admin/device intents, but commit requires validated external authority and witnesses; text naming a capability cannot mint it.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A sufficiently constrained language can safely encode authority directly in model-authored text without a separate runtime authority boundary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial/full-runtime testing demonstrates text-only authority is equally unforgeable and preserves delegation/revocation/audit semantics, or capability-bound lowering cannot express required application classes.
hypotheses.result: Retain current expressibility!=authority invariant; final runtime handle representation remains implementation-gated.
